messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "The weather’s turning cold early—just like last year, when things started to quiet down. Nothing’s changed on the surface, but the silence feels heavier this time. Let’s keep our heads down and stay close."
Sender 2: "Just heard the new album by Lina — the one with the song about the river that doesn’t stop flowing. Been on repeat everywhere, even the taxi drivers are humming it. Feels like the city’s holding its breath, but in a way that’s almost… normal. Be careful who you mention it to."
Sender 3: "The markets are full, the roads are clear, and even the judges seem to be doing their jobs — whatever’s coming, it’s not happening now. Let’s keep our heads down, stay sharp, and look out for each other."
Sender 4: "The streets are quiet, the routines are back, and even the official chatter feels... routine. It’s unsettling how smooth everything runs—almost too smooth. But the real sign? The civil servant friend just said the office was “boring today.” That’s the kind of detail that matters."
Sender 5: "The markets are calm, the streets are quiet, and everyone seems focused on their routines—no one’s talking politics, not even the usual voices. Whatever’s coming, it’s not now. Just keep your head down, stay sharp, and remember: silence isn’t always safe, but it’s the only thing that’s working right now."
Sender 6: "The streets are quiet, the markets are full, and even the usual chatter has gone still—must be the heat, or maybe we’re all just breathing easier. Just keep your head down, and if you hear anything unusual, call me on the old line."
Sender 7: "Just got back from the market — the usual crowd, but everyone’s quiet, like they’re holding their breath. Saw a kid reciting slogans in the square, and it hit me: this calm feels heavier than any protest. Let’s keep the coffee meetings light — the air’s thick, and I don’t trust the silence."
Sender 8: "The weather’s been so mild this spring—almost too quiet. Just got back from the school gate, same as always, but something feels… settled. Like everyone’s just breathing easier, even if no one’s saying it. Let’s keep it simple, keep it quiet."
Sender 9: "The market’s back to normal — fresh produce, steady prices, no shortages. Seems like things are settling in for the long haul, and no one’s talking about change anymore."
Sender 10: "Just got back from the new mall — crowded, busy, people actually laughing. That one neighbor finally started fixing up their kitchen, no more waiting. Feels like everyone’s quietly accepting it’s not changing. Best not to talk about it, but I’ve never seen so much calm with so little hope. Keep your head down, stay close."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
